This section gives a brief overview of the different testing tools. Subsequent chapters dive into running tests and adding new tests . Kinds of tests There are several kinds of tests to exercise things in the Rust distribution. Almost all of them are driven by ./x test , with some exceptions noted below. Compile

nodes.directText: The standard library and many of the compiler packages include typical Rust unit tests, integration tests, and documentation tests. You can pass a path to for almost any package in the or directory, and will essentially run on that package.
nodes.subtreeText: The standard library and many of the compiler packages include typical Rust #[test] unit tests, integration tests, and documentation tests. You can pass a path to ./x test for almost any package in the library/ or compiler/ directory, and x will essentially run cargo test on that package.
Command Description ./x test library/std Runs tests on std only ./x test library/core Runs tests on core only ./x test compiler/rustc_data_structures Runs tests on rustc_data_structures

nodes.directText: The standard library relies very heavily on documentation tests to cover its functionality. However, unit tests and integration tests can also be used as needed. Almost all of the compiler packages have doctests disabled.
nodes.subtreeText: The standard library relies very heavily on documentation tests to cover its functionality. However, unit tests and integration tests can also be used as needed. Almost all of the compiler packages have doctests disabled.

nodes.directText: Tidy is a custom tool used for validating source code style and formatting conventions, such as rejecting long lines. There is more information in the or the .
nodes.subtreeText: Tidy is a custom tool used for validating source code style and formatting conventions, such as rejecting long lines. There is more information in the section on coding conventions or the Tidy Readme .

nodes.directText: Rustfmt is integrated with the build system to enforce uniform style across the compiler. The formatting check is automatically run by the Tidy tool mentioned above.
nodes.subtreeText: Rustfmt is integrated with the build system to enforce uniform style across the compiler. The formatting check is automatically run by the Tidy tool mentioned above.

Command Description ./x fmt --check Checks formatting and exits with an error if formatting is needed. ./x fmt Runs rustfmt across the entire codebase. ./x test tidy --bless First runs rustfmt to format the codebase, then runs tidy checks.

nodes.directText: Packages that are included with Rust have all of their tests run as well. This includes things such as cargo, clippy, rustfmt, miri, bootstrap (testing the Rust build system itself), etc.
nodes.subtreeText: Packages that are included with Rust have all of their tests run as well. This includes things such as cargo, clippy, rustfmt, miri, bootstrap (testing the Rust build system itself), etc.

nodes.directText: Most of the tools are located in the directory. To run the tool’s tests, just pass its path to .
nodes.subtreeText: Most of the tools are located in the src/tools directory. To run the tool’s tests, just pass its path to ./x test .

nodes.directText: Usually these tools involve running within the tool’s directory.
nodes.subtreeText: Usually these tools involve running cargo test within the tool’s directory.

nodes.directText: If you want to run only a specified set of tests, append to the command.
nodes.subtreeText: If you want to run only a specified set of tests, append --test-args FILTER_NAME to the command.

nodes.directText: In CI, some tools are allowed to fail. Failures send notifications to the corresponding teams, and is tracked on the . More information can be found in the .

nodes.directText: Rust tests integration with real-world code to catch regressions and make informed decisions about the evolution of the language. There are several kinds of ecosystem tests, including Crater. See the for more details.
